title: Establish Runtime Certification Service and Canary Driver Rollout
creator: Maya Singh
description: Create a Runtime Certification Service (RCS) that maintains a signed, queryable corpus of certified runtime artifacts (OS image, CUDA version, GPU driver, pinned runtime image, runner config). RCS will be the single source of truth for which combinations are allowed in CI, canary pools, and Dedicated clusters. Alongside RCS we will implement a Canary Driver Rollout pattern that exercises new driver/CUDA/image combos with a synthetic multi-tenant workload to measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, memory stability, and model output consistency before promoting to broad use.
acceptance_criteria: RCS exposes an API endpoint /v1/certified that returns signed entries (image, driver, cuda, kernel-abi, runtime-hash) and a human-readable changelog.
CI gate integrates RCS: any CI job that starts a runner must verify the image+driver combo against RCS and fail fast if un-certified.
Canary harness runs on a dedicated 3-node pool and executes our synthetic workload for every new candidate combo; results saved to Grafana and BigQuery.
Automated regression detector flags a candidate if tokens/sec drops >=6% or p95 latency increases >=10% sustained across 3 consecutive 10-minute windows, or if memory OOMs occur.
On a failed canary the system creates a rollback workflow: auto-open GH issue/PR with repro logs, tag owners, and block promotion to Dedicated/Hosted lanes.
Documentation (Confluence) describing RCS schema, signing flow, canary playbook, and operator runbook is published and reviewed by runtime and infra leads.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (inventory): scan current pinned images and driver combos from /benchmarks, production manifests, and existing pinned-runtime manifests (owner: @liam). Produce canonical CSV and ingest into RCS DB.

Phase 2 (service): lightweight Go service with signing key (KMS) that serves /v1/certified and an admin UI to add/remove entries. Auth via internal mTLS. Implement retention of historical entries for audit.

Phase 3 (canary): extend load harness with a 'syn-conv' workload generator that mimics our tokens/sec distribution and KV-cache reuse patterns; run each candidate for 30 minutes under steady-state traffic and collect token throughput, p50/p95 latency, memory RSS, and kernel GPU errors.

Phase 4 (CI + rollout): CI plugin verifies RCS; CD pipeline queries RCS to decide promotion. Add an automated rollback job that is triggered by the regression detector and wires into GitHub + Slack + PagerDuty.

Instrument regression detection as a small service using EWMA baselines and a sliding window of 10m windows, with configurable thresholds per-model-family. Persist metrics and anomalies to BigQuery and emit Grafana alerts.
Security: signing/verification requires KMS-managed key and periodic rotation. Add a small threat model doc and submit for security review if required.
comments: 2025-01-28 - Maya Singh: Kickoff notes: runtime + infra + benchmarks owners met. Agreed to build a minimal RCS and integrate with existing load harness rather than redesigning the harness. Action items: inventory, prototype API, and prototype syn-conv workload.

2025-02-03 - Liam O'Connor: Inventory complete — found 24 active combos across benchmarks and production. Uploaded csv to drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/runtime-inventory.csv. Noted 3 combos that differ only by kernel ABI (need explicit kernel field).

2025-02-05 - QA: Ran a first-pass canary using syn-conv against driver combo nv-535/cuda-12.1; observed tokens/sec -4% and p95 +3% under 30m run. This is within thresholds; promoting to staged pool for 24h soak.

2025-02-09 - Eng: Prototype RCS service up (branch: github.com/redwood-inference/rcs/tree/prototype). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rcs/pull/12. Basic /v1/certified returns JSON list signed with dev key.

2025-02-11 - Metrics: Implemented EWMA-based detector. During synthetic regression injection test, detector flagged combo when tokens/sec dropped ~7% for three consecutive windows. Created automated rollback PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-config/pull/227.
2025-02-12 - PM (Ana Rodriguez): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Agreed to tighten p95 threshold for conversational models to 8% (from 10%) due to SLA needs. Updated ACs accordingly.
Next steps: finish KMS integration, add auth for admin UI, harden CI plugin, and run a real canary across two model families (chat and embeddings) by 2025-02-25.
